success_patterns: The clue was a near-verbatim paraphrase of a dictionary or glossary definition in one passage ('An industrial unit of production equal to the work one person can produce in...'). The agent matched the definition wording, took the headword of that entry ('Man-hours - definition of Man-hours', 'man hour: a common unit of labor...'), and answered with the singular term in the context's own form. It did not describe the unit or pick a nearby term such as 'hour' or 'minute'.

patch.reasoning: Definition-style clues ('This unit is equal to...', 'a word meaning...') are common in Jeopardy-style sets. The context often has a dictionary or glossary snippet whose definition matches the clue and whose headword is the answer. Rule 3 covers archive layouts and slot-blank sentences but not this case. A short addition tells the agent to match the definition wording and answer with the headword, not the definition's component words (hour, minute, unit).

edits.target: - Archive lines may also be formatted 'CATEGORY | clue text | answer'. Take the answer that follows the clue, even if the whole context is one short passage.
edits.content: - Definition-style clues ('This unit is equal to...', 'a term for...') often match a dictionary or glossary snippet whose wording nearly equals the clue. The answer is that entry's HEADWORD (the title such as 'Man-hours - definition of...', or the bolded term before the colon), not a word inside the definition ('man-hour', not 'hour' or 'minute'). Give it in singular, in the spelling the passage uses.
